name: Flood-Net
tagline: The engineering register and toolset for the Bureau's Queensland flood-warning radio network: stations, repeaters, health, field work.
about: Flood-Net is the register and toolset for the Bureau of Meteorology's Queensland (and neighbouring) flood-warning telemetry network: the field stations, the repeaters that relay them, the base stations and the radio paths between. It is a browser app with no build step, backed by a Supabase Postgres database and a Cloudflare Worker at floodwarning.net, for the people who plan, inspect and keep the network running. It takes readings in from base stations, judges the network's health on a schedule, publishes a daily animated bulletin, and serves public station data to AI agents through a read-only API and MCP server. It is not a flood warning service.
kind: web app, Cloudflare Worker and Postgres database

components.name: App shell and offline
components.what: The single page: about 58 tabs in 13 groups, sign-in, the station list's three sources, the service worker; index.html's script order is the contract and every app push bumps the ?v= stamp.

components.name: Stations, maps and 3-D
components.what: The Stations tab and its map layers, the station card and editor, the digital twin, path profiles and link budgets, printed radio path maps, Look Around and Nearby.

components.name: Network, RF and interference
components.what: ALERT IDs, Repeaters and Repeater Delays; the ACMA register, RF Changes and the Interference Workbench; Reception Map and Bit-Flip Sources; Signal Routes, Network Review, the ALERT2 Transition Plan and the TDMA Planner.

components.name: Decoders and Serial Monitor
components.what: The ALERT, ALERT2, HFEM and Quansheng codecs, the off-air SDR decoder, and the Serial Monitor whose receiver cards post what they decode, plus the sdr-pi relay for an RTL-SDR on a Pi.

components.name: Readings and network health
components.what: Station Health, Backbone, Investigations and Methodology, the Base Stations tab that manages RPi ALERT stations, and the Field Data, Message Log and Plots tabs over the readings; findings are worked out on the server every 15 minutes.

components.name: Teams and tasks
components.what: Teams (each hub's staff, Property Services, Radio licensing, the SoRT Forum and the rest) and the tasks handed to them, each at a station with a status, a due date and a thread of notes; a roster seen only by its own people and administrators, a task only by its team, its maker and the people who hand out tasks; and the SoRT scope builder's #tasks= hand-off, reviewed before anything is made.

components.name: Network bulletins and voices
components.what: A scheduled Claude session writes a two-minute animated bulletin each weekday morning (and weekly on Mondays), drawn on Station Health and voiced by the Droggies through ElevenLabs.

components.name: Site visits, surveying and training
components.what: Inspection sheets, site maintenance and inspection history, the Field Camera and Field Photos, level surveys and two-peg tests, field training and the knowledge base.

components.name: floodwarning.net Worker
components.what: The Cloudflare Worker in front of the app: Access sign-in turned into a database session, the /api/db proxy for networks that block Supabase, photos and the data archive in R2, Ask Claude, bug reports, council cameras, road routes, push and scheduled notifications.

components.name: Agent API and MCP server
components.what: Read-only public station data for AI agents and scripts: REST at /api/v1 with OpenAPI, MCP at /api/mcp, rate limited, with a changelog and an email list for its changes.

components.name: Postgres schema (Supabase)
components.what: The meganet schema: stations, readings, receptions and their roll-ups, inspections, photos, health findings, ingest tokens, base stations, teams and tasks, in 95 numbered migrations applied by the db-migrate workflow; every raw day archived to R2 before it is deleted.

components.name: MQTT bridge and base-station logger
components.what: The MQTT-to-ingest bridge (Fly.io, deployed by a workflow button) and the CRBasic program for a base station's datalogger that posts over HTTPS and publishes over MQTT.

components.name: Scheduled jobs, agent skills and data tools
components.what: GitHub workflows (smoke test, ACMA refresh, photo syncs, station snapshot, roadmap sync), the CI doctor and photo reader Claude skills, the weekly security review, the ingest tools and the test suite.

provides.name: Agent API (REST and MCP)
provides.what: Read-only public station data: search and stations near a point, a station's record and dossier, readings and the latest reading per station, health findings and silent stations, flood levels, service levels, ACMA licences, a station's radio path to the base stations with the fade margin saved for each hop, catchments, networks, and a changelog of every visible API change.

provides.name: HTTPS ingest for base stations
provides.what: PostgREST RPCs a base station calls with its own token: ingest_http (readings, deduplicated on address, time and raw value), report_ingest_point, report_receptions, and asking for a token that an administrator approves; reachable directly or through the floodwarning.net /api/db proxy.

provides.name: Base-station check-in
provides.what: A base station's minute-by-minute health report (receivers, queue, power, clock, software, spectrum) and the short fixed list of requests the Base Stations tab can leave for it: a setting, a restart, an update, its log, the team's SSH keys.

provides.name: Station list
provides.what: Every station with its sensors, ALERT addresses, repeaters and radio details; kept in Postgres (meganet.stations_doc) and exported weekly to stations.json in the same shape.

provides.name: Off-air ALERT decoder
provides.what: Decodes legacy ALERT (Binary, Enhanced iFLOWS, ASCII) from SDR samples, with carrier offset; a port of agmurf/sdr-alert-decoder (MIT), with a real off-air test capture.

provides.name: Quansheng ALERT radio codec
provides.what: The serial codec for the Quansheng UV-K5 V3 / UV-K1 ALERT receiver firmware (schema 2): its records, its console commands and the station table it keeps.

provides.name: ALERT2 / ERT-A2 parser
provides.what: Reads the ELPRO ERT-A2's RS-232 ASCII lines and USB binary frames by the NHWC specifications, including self-reports.

provides.name: NMEA GPS parser
provides.what: NMEA 0183 GGA, RMC and GST sentences from a serial GPS.

provides.name: ALERT / ERTS packet formats
provides.what: The ALERT / ERTS frame decoder and encoder and its FORMATS table, per the Bureau's ERTS Data Formats specification.

provides.name: ALERT2 transition plan figures
provides.what: The planning figures and costs in the ALERT2 Transition Plan (equipment, site audits, licensing per network change).

provides.name: Bulletin voicing
provides.what: How the bulletins read the Droggies' cast (voice, model, direction, sustain, tempo) and the Bulletin voices workflow that voices each bulletin.

consumes.what: Each presenter's voice, read from the Droggies' published site on every Bulletin voices run.
consumes.on_change: A recast needs nothing: the next bulletin is voiced with it (run Actions > Bulletin voices to re-voice old ones). A new or renamed field: update tools/voice/speak.mjs and run cd test && npm run bulletin.

consumes.what: The presenters' names, roles and sign-off lines copied into health-bulletin.js ROSTER and tools/bulletin/validate.mjs PRESENTERS, and their portraits cropped into assets/presenters/.
consumes.on_change: Update ROSTER in health-bulletin.js and PRESENTERS in tools/bulletin/validate.mjs, re-crop a changed portrait into assets/presenters/, run cd test && npm run bulletin, and bump the version stamp.

consumes.what: The latest RPi ALERT release, shown beside each base station's version on the Base Stations tab (amber when a station is behind).
consumes.on_change: Nothing: the tab asks GitHub every five minutes while open.

consumes.what: RPi ALERT's SDR channel plan (each stick's sample-rate windows and usable band), mirrored in base-stations.js WINDOWS and the waterfall's edges, and in sdr-pi.js's channel rules.
consumes.on_change: Match WINDOWS in base-stations.js (and sdr-pi.js where the rule is shared) to the new RATES and USABLE; run cd test && npm run basestations && npm run sdrpi; bump the version stamp.

consumes.what: The weekly security review reads RPi ALERT's agent and Pi image beside Flood-Net, because the two trust each other through ingest tokens and Base Stations requests.
consumes.on_change: Nothing by hand: the Monday review (tools/security-scan/brief.md) reads it and files findings in flood-net-private.

consumes.what: The radio's USB serial protocol (schema 2) and its station-table format, which quansheng.js implements and serial-radio.js builds from the loaded station list; sdr-pi.js follows the same line rules.
consumes.on_change: Bring quansheng.js (and serial-radio.js / sdr-pi.js where a rule is shared) into line with the changed sections; run cd test && npm run quansheng && npm run sdrpi; bump the version stamp.

consumes.what: The historical inspection workbook and its derived files, read by the inspection ingest tools from a clone beside this one (tools/ingest/private.py) and loaded into the database.
consumes.on_change: Re-run the inspection tools in tools/ingest (survey.py, extract.py, crosswalk.py, remarks.py, load.py) against the clone; their checks run in flood-net-private's own workflow.

consumes.what: The ALERT / ERTS packet decoder and encoder, ported once into the ALERT Packets tab (packets.js) and developed here since.
The national ALERT address file and the Bureau's ERTS Data Formats specification, kept byte-for-byte as data/All 2021 Working 2.txt and docs/BOM spec erts_data_formats_doc.pdf.
consumes.on_change: Copy the changed file over data/All 2021 Working 2.txt (read by packets.js and serial-radio.js) or the PDF in docs/.

consumes.what: The QLD Globe recipes for the LiDAR contour and survey-mark layers: which ArcGIS services, sublayers resolved by name, and the server-rendered approach (map-contours.js, map-survey.js).

The SoRT scope builder's hand-off of a forum's agreed jobs for a station: it opens floodwarning.net/#tasks=<base64url of UTF-8 JSON, v 1>, and the Tasks tab reviews them — each task's team picked by the hub or the team name SoRT gives, de-duplicated by sort:<session>:<ref> — making nothing until somebody who hands out tasks presses Create (tasks.js, parseHandoff).
consumes.on_change: Read SoRT's payload as v2/js/tasks.js now writes it and bring tasks.js's parseHandoff() and test/tasks.mjs up to it. A payload with a new v needs a reader of its own beside v 1's, which links already sent still carry.
